description:
Find claims from a natural-language question.

    The first stage is a lexical match on the content phrases. When that match is empty, shorter literal phrases are tried, then a small list of scientific synonyms. A keyword with no function word stays on the lexical match and does not expand.
    Question hits stay on strategy question. fallback is keyword for a shorter literal phrase and expanded for synonyms. Rank is relevance to the question: a matched phrase outranks scattered words, and evidence strength breaks ties.
    notice is no_matching_claims when nothing matches. notice is no_evidence when every returned hit has an empty excerpt. A hit with an empty excerpt says no evidence in match_reason.
    Each hit includes match_reason, source_url, doi, and paper_id when those are known, up to two supporting claims, and one contradicting claim when one is stored. Each related claim carries that same compact pointer. unpublished is true for a private unpublished paper. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.

    A domain keeps claims whose primary domain is that value or one of its
    aliases. cross_domain also keeps claims from other domains that carry
    the domain as a secondary tag.

    Use this when the input is a question instead of keywords.
    Example: search_smart(natural_language="How do transformers handle long context?", domain="ai-ml", limit=5).
    Example: search_smart(natural_language="What causes LLM hallucinations in RAG systems?", limit=5).

cross_domain.description: Also return claims from other primary domains that carry this domain as a secondary tag. Default false.
cross_domain.title: Cross Domain

domain.description: Primary domain or an alias of it. Example: ai-ml.
domain.title: Domain

natural_language.description: A question or description of the claims you want. Example: How do transformers handle long context?
examples: How do transformers handle long context?
natural_language.title: Natural Language

offset.description: Number of hits to skip. Example: 0.
offset.title: Offset

name: search_smart

contradicting.description: One stored contradicting claim, when one is present, with the same compact source pointer.

doi.description: Stored DOI, the DataCite DOI of an arXiv id, or a bioRxiv paper id that is already a DOI. Empty when unknown. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
doi.title: Doi

match_reason.description: Why this hit ranked here: keyword overlap, domain match, and evidence strength.
match_reason.title: Match Reason

paper_id.description: Stored paper id when one is known. A private paper is an opaque private-paper id. Empty when unknown. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
paper_id.title: Paper Id

source_url.description: Stable link to the paper when one is known. Empty when the claim has no pointer. Full provenance stays on get_evidence.
source_url.title: Source Url

supporting.description: Up to two other claims from the same papers. Each has claim_id, statement, strength, and the same compact source pointer.
supporting.title: Supporting

unpublished.description: True when this claim is from a private unpublished paper. Public sources stay false.
unpublished.title: Unpublished

RelatedClaim.description: One claim shown beside a search hit.

doi.description: Stored DOI, the DataCite DOI of an arXiv id, or a bioRxiv paper id that is already a DOI. Empty when unknown.
doi.title: Doi

paper_id.description: Stored paper id. A private paper is an opaque private-paper id. Empty when unknown.
paper_id.title: Paper Id

source_url.description: Stable link to that claim's paper when one is known. Empty when it has no pointer.
source_url.title: Source Url

unpublished.description: True when that claim is from a private unpublished paper.
unpublished.title: Unpublished

RelatedClaim.title: RelatedClaim

outputSchema.description:
question matches content phrases. lexical is a keyword query.

fallback is keyword when a shorter literal phrase supplied the hits, and
expanded when those hits come from scientific synonyms. notice is
no_matching_claims when the query matches nothing, and no_evidence when
every returned hit has an empty excerpt.

notice.description: no_matching_claims when the query matches nothing. no_evidence when every returned hit has an empty excerpt. Null when the hits include evidence text.
notice.title: Notice

outputSchema.title: SmartSearchResult
